facts.statement: The only known species of Kaiika is Kaiika maxwelli.
The fossil was discovered in 1998 by Dr. Phillip Maxwell in the Kauru Formation near the Waihao River in New Zealand.
facts.quote: It was found in 1998 by Dr Phillip Maxwell, a paleontologist and stratigrapher, from the Kauru Formation of the Canterbury Basin, near the Waihao River.

facts.statement: The genus was formally described and named by Ewan Fordyce and Daniel Thomas in 2011.
facts.quote: It was first named by Ewan Fordyce and Daniel Thomas in 2011

facts.statement: The entire genus is known from a single fossil humerus bone.
facts.quote: It is known only from a single humerus.

facts.statement: Kaiika was an early penguin that lived in South Canterbury, New Zealand, during the Early Eocene epoch.
facts.quote: Kaiika (Māori for "eater of fish") is an extinct genus of basal penguin from Early Eocene (Waipawan-Mangaorapan subage) deposits of South Canterbury, New Zealand.

facts.statement: Kaiika lived between 56 and 48.9 million years ago during the Ypresian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Kaiika represents one of the oldest known penguin species.
facts.quote: Kaiika is one of the oldest penguins known.
